section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "Like an eagle stirring its nest...", linking it to guarding Israel as the pupil of God's eye, and the superiority of Israel over angels.
section.t: "Like an eagle stirring its nest, hovering over its young, He spreads His wings, takes it, bears it on His pinions. God alone leads him..."
And this refers to what is stated earlier,
"He guards him as the pupil of His eye."
That through this—that He guards him as the pupil of His eye—through this, "like an eagle stirring its nest,"
and therefore, "He spreads His wings, takes it, bears it on His pinions. God alone leads him."
And the explanation of "He guards him as the pupil of His eye":
It is known
that there are Sefiros and angels that are called by the name "eyes,"
and as explained in Torah Ohr
regarding the matter of "the eyes of God roaming and roving," which are two types among the angels.
However, Israel, who are innermost relative to the ministering angels, are the aspect of the "pupil of His eye."
For the eye, although it is a vessel for the power of sight,
nevertheless, the essence of sight is from the pupil within the eye.
And this is the superiority of Israel over the angels:
that the angels are called by the name "eyes" in general,
and Israel are the aspect of the "pupil of His eye."
